Concern for Tribals.
The students of our Vidyalaya visited a Tribal Colony in Wynad to
hand over medicines, clothes and money. The money would be
utilized to construct a well, the group had an interaction with the
tribal elders and children and could gain an idea of their way of
life.
The students contributed willingly to purchase iron tablets, which
were supplied to the tribal women of Attappady, where poverty is
endemic.
Responding positively towards the appeal made by Sri.Vijay Menon
during his talk on 15-6-2015 students of 11th Std. generously
contributed an amount of Rs.14,595/- for buying sleeping mats for
the Tribals of Wyanad District. These mats were handed over to
the representatives.

Kerala Piravi was celebrated in the Vidyalaya with enthralling
programmes perfomed by children on 1st November 2016. A few
children recited poems in Malayalam which was an audio feast on
this apt day. A map of Kerala state was displayed in which each
district was decorated with different pulses and grains. .A debate
on the 'Changing Culture of Kerala' was conducted by students.
ONV Krupp's famous poem 'AMMA' was enacted in a typical Kerala
dance form which was a feast to the eye and ear.
Three non teaching staff of the Vidyalaya ,Sri Mohanan ,Sri
Ayappan and ,Sri Krishnadas were felicitated on this occasion by
Director of Education Dr. G Mukundan in the presence of Principal,
Vice Principal and Head mistress.

Chinmaya Birth Centenary
The Chinmaya Birth Centenary celebrations grand finale was held
in the Chinmaya Janmashathabdi Nagar near Neeranjali hall on the
21st and the 22nd May. The Chief Guest of the day was Justice A
Hari Prasad of the Kerala High Court. Padmasree P. R.
Krishnakumar, chancellor, Avinasalingam University was a special
guest. Adv. Therambil Ramakrishnan offered felicitations. Dr.
G.Mukundan, Director of Education, Chinmaya Vidyalaya and Chief
Sevak, Chinmaya Seva Trust, Kerala, presented mementos to the
dignitaries. Sri .P. Krishnakumar, General Convener, welcomed the
gathering and Sri T.M Reghunandan, Treasurer, Chinmaya Seva
Trust, Kerala offered the vote of thanks.
Eminent speakers like Swami Chidanandapuri, Sri Gopalakrishnan
Vaidik, Sri Rahul Easwer, Sri Vijaya Menon etc. to name a few
graced the occasion. The valedictory function was on 22nd May,
the Chief Guest being Padmasree Dr. Sunder Menon. Acharyas,
Chief Sevaks and all the teachers behind the cultural programmes
were honoured.

Thrissur and Dr Ramesh Kumar (Consultant District Hospital
Thrissur) addressed the students based on the queries they had
placed. The talk focused on their right to know about themselves,
their adolescence and their sexuality basic facts on HIV and other
ST's develop and reinforce life skills that enable them to protect
themselves dispel myths and clarify misconceptions and so on. In a
nutshell, the torque provided the students with the basic accurate
knowledge about adolescence, sex and sexuality which they have

Samanvayam
The annual Fun, Food and games Carnival "Samanvayam
was held in the Vidyalaya on 29 th January 2019. It was a
gala event where the students get an opportunity to
develop various soft skills like negotiating, marketing,
advertising and at the same time displaying their food
items artisitically in various stalls which have been
creatively christened. There are food items which can tickle
anyones taste buds and also a member of innovative and
fun filled games that literally take your breath away.
Another talk was conducted exclusively for the students of
the commerce stream by Sri M Satyakumar on the topic
Designing Career, Transforming India. He discussed in
simple language the dilemma in opting for a subject for and
after the plus two level and the plethora of opportunities
available for commerce graduates. He was able to create a
good rapport with the students and received great
appreciation from them.

World Environment Day
The day was observed in the Vidyalaya on June 6th. Our
Honourable Chief Guest Smt. Jalaja S. Menon, Assistant Professor,
Kerala Agricultural University addressed the students emphasizing
the need to conserve soil and to protect wildlife. She was
presented with a memento comprising of a paper bag, seeds, and
vermicompost packet and sandal wood sapling. A poster making
competition along with a Rangoli competition was held and the
winners were presented with ginger saplings. The assembly ended
with a pledge to protect the environment.
